found.quote: Unauthorised use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)

Unauthorised use of Gen AI includes but is not limited to the use of a Gen AI tool to generate any form of submitted work that a learner submits without proper acknowledgment of that tool’s use in its generation.

Presenting text, digital work (e.g. computer code or programs), video recordings or images copied with only minor changes from sources such as the internet, the output of GenAI, books, journals or any other media, without due acknowledgement;

The presenting or making use of fictitious, altered or misrepresented data, evidence, references, citations or experimental results and includes the use of GenAI created content or output that is fabricated or

Unauthorised content generation is “the production of academic work, in whole or in part, for academic credit, progression or award, whether or not a payment or other favour is involved, using unapproved or undeclared human or technological assistance”.
Learners are authors of any work they submit and bear responsibility for its content, accuracy and integrity.

In the completion of any work submitted for assessment the learner is responsible for critiquing its output in terms of logic, consistency, accuracy and bias. This includes where GenAI is used as authorised.
Where GenAI use is permitted, any such declaration by a learner should enable those assessing it to evaluate the authenticity and quality of the work being submitted.

Such a declaration should specify the exact name and version of the GenAI system(s) used, a clear description of how those system(s) were used, the prompting strategy used and specify the steps taken to validate the system’s outputs.
The RCSI Library’s guides and tutorials including those on EndNote®, Referencing and GenAI
In particular, the use of AI for any placement activity must be in accordance with both this policy and approved by the student’s supervisor or equivalent in the relevant placement setting.
a supportive approach to addressing their shortcomings with regard to demonstrating academic integrity will be adopted by the University.
As part of the investigation, the student may be asked to participate in an oral assessment of their work as submitted.
If the suspected breach appears to warrant a Level 3 response, the matter is referred to Registry for further consideration under the Disciplinary Regulations.

a breach of academic integrity associated with academic misconduct of a serious nature involves any behaviour or activity, which would likely have the effect of more than marginally enhancing the grade or outcome awarded to the student
Any determination made in accordance with the provisions of this policy may be reviewed in accordance with the appeal provisions of the University’s Disciplinary Regulations.

unsure.quote: If a student is in doubt as to what constitutes academic integrity, they are encouraged to seek advice and guidance from a member of the academic staff.
unsure.why: Academic integrity generally, not AI use specifically

unsure.quote: The RCSI Academic Council requires all students to successfully complete the RCSI online Academic Integrity resource on at least one occasion while completing their studies.
unsure.why: General integrity training, not tied to AI use

unsure.quote: RCSI reserves the right to avail of any technological or other means available to it to detect academic misconduct
unsure.why: Detection means mentioned without naming AI use

unsure.quote: a Level 1, 2 or 3 response with or without an accompanying sanction (e.g. grade penalty) or corrective action (e.g. re-submit assignment).

unsure.quote: under the oversight of the Academic Integrity Committee
unsure.why: Policy review oversight; AI only as a review trigger
